elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM05-E01 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating Arabic and English texts and noticing unfamiliar words or expressions, and reflecting on challenges associated with transferring meaning from one language to another

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM05-E02 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing translations of the same text, commenting on similarities and differences between versions, and considering possible reasons for these

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM05-E03 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on the importance of non-verbal elements of communication, such as hand gestures, head movements and facial expressions, and how these are sometimes used to mean different things in different cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM05-E04 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying culturally specific vocabulary and expressions such as تقبّل فائق الاحترام, and discussing strategies for choosing words that best reflect the intended meaning and context

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM05-E05 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: paraphrasing English words or expressions that have no equivalent in Arabic, such as ‘brainstorm’, ‘selfie’ or ‘fundraiser’

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM05-E06 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating information from different sources for relevance and cultural appropriateness, for example, facts from reliable websites versus social media or word-of-mouth, and discussing potential issues that may arise from using inaccurate information

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM05-E07 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
identifying and discussing how values or attitudes are reflected in Arabic and English, including the concepts of time and punctuality reflected in language such as لا تستعجل، لنلتقي السّاعة الثامنة تماما, as well as in social interactions such as expressing indirect thanks, apologies or appreciation, for example,

.أشكرك شكرا جزيلا على جهودك الرائعة. لا شكر على واجب
تقبّل مني أصدق الإعتذار؛ أعتذر على الخطأ الذي بدر مني

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM05-E08 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on the difficulty of achieving equivalence in translations of creative texts such as poems, songs and film clips, identifying words and phrases that require particular elaboration or explanation

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM05-E09 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying similarities and differences between their own ways of communicating and interactions between young Arabic speakers in different contexts, such as the expression of politeness or turn-taking in conversations

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM05-E10 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
exploring a range of Arabic and English idioms and proverbs, and discussing the social and cultural values and perspectives they reflect, for example,

من جدَ وجد، ومن زرع حصد

من سار على الدرب وصل

الوقت كالسيف إن لم تقطعه قطعك

!ليس الفقير من فقد الذهب، بل الفقير فقير العلم والأدب

!الحاجة أمّ الاختراع

!في التأني السّلامة وفي العجلة النّدامة

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LA10CM06 - Arabic 7-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts, selecting vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures and textual conventions for familiar and some unfamiliar contexts and purposes, to engage different audiences

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM06-E01 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
presenting persuasive texts such as posters, advertisements or the script of a speech on topics such as recycling, sustainability or circular fashion, for various audiences, for example,

...إنه من الضروري أن نحافظ على البيئة بعدة طرق؛ منها إعادة التدوير، و

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM06-E02 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
informing others in the school community about an issue of interest, call to action, or upcoming events in texts such as notices and newsletter announcements, for example,

إعلان هام
ستحتفل مدرستنا بيوم المعلّم العالمي يوم الإثنين القادم في صالة المدرسة 
نرحب بحضور الجميع
المأكولات السريعة وأضرارها؛ الألعاب الإلكترونية وتأثيرها السّلبي على العائلة

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM06-E03 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
creating a multimodal resource to introduce Arabic-speaking tourists or recent migrants to different features and aspects of Australian life such as cultural and linguistic diversity, local attractions, animals, dangers and outback exploration, for example,

أماكن سياحية رائعة كدار الاوبرا والجبال الزرقاء في في أستراليا

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM06-E04 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a journal entry or contributing to a school newsletter in Arabic reflecting on a visit to an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place, and, with permission, referring to cultural knowledge of the site’s significance

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM06-E05 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
researching a popular tourist site or attraction in an Arabic-speaking country and writing about a traveller’s experience in the third person, for example,

سافر سمير إلى البتراء وشاهد المعابد التّراثيّة القديمة والجِمال في الصحراء

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM06-E06 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
reporting on their own and others’ experiences such as holidays or a school camp, for example,

بالنسبة لي الرحلة كانت ممتعة بينما بعض التلاميذ شعروا بالملل؛ بالرغم من الساعات الطويلة التي قضيناها في الطريق إلا إنني لم أشعر بالتّعب لكن أصدقائي كانوا متعَبين

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM06-E07 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
writing a procedure for younger students to follow, with steps and diagrams, such as dances or recipes, for example,

التّبولة

.افرم البقدونس والنعنع والبندورة

.أضف عصير الليمون والملح والزيت والبرغل

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM06-E08 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
creating a video tour of the school for Arabic-speaking exchange students or new students, with commentary about the classrooms, subjects, canteen menu and facilities, for example,

الطعام في المقصف لذيذ جدا؛ الرّياضة مادّة مهمة

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM06-E09 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
creating alternative versions of traditional Arabic stories by introducing new characters, new scenes or different endings, for example,

ألف ليلة وليلة؛ سندباد

elaborations.name: VC2LA10CM06-E10 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
expressing imagined experiences in texts such as poems and video clips that relate to significant celebrations or events in both Australia and the Arabic-speaking world, for example,

عيد الأم؛ عيد الشّهداء؛ العيد الوطني الأسترالي؛ الأعياد الدينية

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LA10UL01 - Arabic 7-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply features and conventions of spoken Arabic to enhance and extend fluency, and to respond to and create a range of texts in familiar and unfamiliar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL01-E01 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: pronouncing words that include الشّدة، والتّنوين، والسكون and using them appropriately in sentences and texts

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL01-E02 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising features of the Arabic sound system, discriminating tones, rhythm and sound flow, such as the words with 3 small syllables ك/ت/ب, words with a long syllable قا/لَ , words with an extended syllable آمين, words with a closed syllable يكتب, and words with 2 closed syllables يستخرج, applying prior knowledge of pronunciation and sound conventions to predict the spelling and sound of unfamiliar words during class dictation or while reading aloud or transcribing a text

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL01-E03 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the rhythms of the Arabic language, including intonation, tone and stress, to increase fluency, emphasise emotions, indicate the purpose of the phrase (e.g. interrogative or statement), and enhance expression

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL01-E04 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the need for pauses or changes of tone in complex sentences with embedded clauses

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL01-E05 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to a range of audio texts at various speeds, such as phone messages and announcements, to develop strategies and techniques to infer meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL01-E06 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
noticing how intonation and tone of voice can convey emotions and shade meaning, such as distinguishing between colloquial and formal language, for example,

حقا؟؛ يا إلهي!؛ تعال إلى هنا حالا

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL01-E07 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
using onomatopoeia in sentences for literary effect in texts such as comics and stories, for example,

...بوم بوم! أسمع أصوات الألعاب النارية في ليلة رأس السنة

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL01-E08 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
reciting difficult tongue twisters or making their own, to improve pronunciation, fluency and pace, for example,

روحي وروحك يا روحي روحين بروح مطرح متروح روحك روحي بتروح
قفص قصب في قفص خشب

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LA10UL02 - Arabic 7-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of context and grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts that include some complex structures, ideas and conventions appropriate to formality and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL02-E01 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying punctuation and spacing rules between words and using their knowledge of writing conventions such as paragraphing and sequencing to create texts, and typing in Arabic

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL02-E02 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that certain letters in Arabic appear in different variations, such as ت، ة

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL02-E03 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
using plural demonstrative pronouns and pronouns such as ‘we’, ‘you’ and ‘they’ in Arabic, for example,

نحن مدرّسون؛ هم طلّاب؛ هذا طالب مجتهد؛ هؤلاء الطّلاب

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL02-E04 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
expanding their knowledge of noun–adjective agreement, for example,

هؤلاء معلّمون بارعون؛ هؤلاء طالبات مجتهدات

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL02-E05 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
identifying possession (e.g. iḍaafa) and attached possessive pronouns for singular and plural, for example,

هذا بيت يوسف / هذا بيته؛ هذا سريري؛ هذه غرفتك؛ كتابك؛ حقيبة نور / هذه حقيبتها؛ صف التلاميذ / صفوفكم؛ سيارة العائلة

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL02-E06 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
using سوف/س with the present tense to express future plans, for example,

سوف أذهب إلى الجامعة؛ سأسافر مع أهلي؛ سوف أشتري سيارة؛ سوف أعمل في مطعم

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL02-E07 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
using a range of conjunctions such as لكن، أو، ف to connect sentences, for example,

لم تذهب سارة لكن هيفاء ذهبت؛ كلّ فطيرة أو كعكة

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL02-E08 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
using interrogative words and expressions, for example,

لم أنت هنا؟؛ هل تريد هذا الكتاب؟

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL02-E09 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
using the subjunctive mood to express doubt, uncertainty or emotion, for example,

قد أسافر في العطلة؛ ربما نذهب يوم السبت الى السينما

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL02-E10 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
describing people and objects, using comparatives and superlatives, for example,

هذا أقلّ من ذاك؛ الكتاب أخفّ من القاموس؛ الماء أفضل من المشروبات الغازية

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL02-E11 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
applying rules of negation in a range of sentences, for example,

لن أتّصل بك؛ لم أتأخر عن الدرس؛ ليس عندي وقت

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL02-E12 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
using imperative verb forms to persuade, encourage, and give advice, for example,

تابع مجهودك؛ حاول مرّة ثانية؛ هيّا يا سامر لنذهب إلى المعلّم ونسأله،؛ لا تعاشر اصحاب السوء لأنهم يضيّعون وقتك

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL02-E13 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
using a range of irregular adjectives to describe number, shape and colour, for example,

قميص أحمر؛ حقيبة حمراء؛ قلم أخضر؛ ممحاة خضراء؛ شكل مدور/مثلث/مربع/مستطيل

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL02-E14 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
using adverbial phrases to expand on ideas and provide further information, for example,

متأخرا؛ باكرا؛ دائما؛ مسرعا

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL02-E15 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
applying appropriate gender for numbers, for example,

خمسة أقلام؛ خمس ساعات؛ ثلاث طالبات؛ ثلاثة طلاب

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LA10UL03 - Arabic 7-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: reflect on and evaluate Arabic texts, using metalanguage to discuss language structures and features

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL03-E01 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the significance and cultural importance of features of different types of texts in Arabic and English, such as forms of address or language associated with rituals or celebrations, and understanding how these vary according to the context, occasion and intended audience

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL03-E02 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
using metalanguage to identify grammatical similarities and differences between Arabic and English, such as word order, sentence types, verb moods, verb tenses, possessive pronouns, gender agreement and script, for example,

وسيم يقرأ الكتاب؛ وردة جميلة؛ باب البيت؛ كتاب الطالب

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL03-E03 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing persuasive texts such as advertisements, slogans or speeches, recognising the use of rhetorical devices and emotive language to engage the intended audience

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL03-E04 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing and explaining differences in text structure and grammar between formal and informal Arabic and English use (e.g. a business letter vs. an informal email)

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL03-E05 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
comparing spoken and written forms of familiar types of texts in Arabic and English such as spoken and written apologies, spoken storytelling and written reports, noticing differences in grammatical, expressive and textual features, for example,

من فضلك اقبل إعتذاري؛ أعتذر/ أقدّم إعتذاري؛ أنا آسف / آسفة

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LA10UL04 - Arabic 7-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: reflect on and explain how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), beliefs, attitudes and values, and how these affect ways of communicating
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL04-E01 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
reflect on and explain how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), beliefs, attitudes and values, and how greetings and expressions in Arabic are used to communicate for specific purposes and in specific situations, for example,

السّلام عليكم؛ في أمان الله؛ الحمد لله؛ مرحبا؛ أهلا وسهلا؛ اشرب الشّاي

...سمير يقرأ قصّة خياليّة وليلى تقرأ مقالة بالجريدة؛ ذهب المدرّسون والمدرّسات إلى المدرسة

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL04-E02 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing language and cultural practices that are interconnected, for example, by identifying religious origins or connotations associated with places such as مكّة المكّرمة، الأزهر الشّريف، حريصا، دير كربلاء، المدينة المنوّرة or by identifying ways in which the residual influences of traditional lifestyles are preserved in language

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL04-E03 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on the protocols required to authentically co-create an Acknowledgement of Country or Place with an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander person, to present and explain in Arabic to a group of Arabic-speaking visitors at a school assembly

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL04-E04 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text:
examining the meaning of Arabic proverbs and sayings, and how they reflect traditional cultural views, ideas and attitudes, for example,

الصديق وقت الضيق؛ أنا وأخي على ابن عمي وأنا وابن عمي على الغريب
العقل السليم في الجسم السليم؛ عصفور باليد أحسن من عشرة على الشجرة

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL04-E05 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing texts created for different audiences in diverse Arabic-speaking regions and countries, noticing how language reflects the priorities, values, beliefs and identities of specific communities

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL04-E06 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying words used in colloquial Arabic that fuse Arabic and English, such as in film, media or advertising, to capture trends, convey concepts, and engage with intercultural experiences, for example, جوجل، شير، هاشتاج، لايك

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL04-E07 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that Arabic carries histories of contact with other languages and cultures, for example, by identifying and classifying loan words or terms that originate from other languages that have been ‘Arabised’ (ta’reeb), such as أطلس، ساندويتش، بيتزا، أوتوبيس، طماطم، ترام

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL04-E08 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the nature and use of the Arabic language in different contexts, and interviewing bilingual people about the experience of using more than one language, for example, by asking an Arabic-speaking person in Australia, ‘When do you use Arabic or English?’; ‘With whom, how and why?’; ‘Do you identify more strongly with one language?’; and ‘Do you express yourself differently in each language?’

elaborations.name: VC2LA10UL04-E09 - Arabic 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating their own cultural and linguistic biographies to discover more about family heritage, migration and history, and reflecting on how this can contribute to their identity and understanding of family beliefs and values
